questions.question: Loading and unloading a school bus:

options.text: Can be dangerous for students.
Does not need an adult watching.
Should happen while refueling.
Can happen while the driver talks to another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be dangerous for students.
questions.explanation: More students are hurt or killed during loading and unloading than while riding the bus. Drivers must follow safety rules and watch carefully during these times.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must be able to do all of the following about oil, except:

options.text: Show where the dipstick is.
Show that the oil level is safe.
Show that the oil level is above the refill mark.
Show that the oil level is below the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that the oil level is below the refill mark.
questions.explanation: You must show where the dipstick is, that the oil level is safe, and that the oil level is above the refill mark. You should NOT show that the oil is below the refill mark.

questions.question: Outside convex mirrors on a bus are located:

options.text: Below the outside flat mirrors.
Above the outside flat mirrors.
Next to the door.
On top of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Below the outside flat mirrors.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are located below the flat mirrors. They help the driver see a wide area around the bus, including traffic, clearance, and students.

questions.question: A properly adjusted convex mirror should let the driver see:

options.text: The entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts.
The front of the bus.
The rear door of the bus.
The top of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts.
questions.explanation: The convex mirror should be adjusted so the driver can see one traffic lane on each side of the bus, the entire side of the bus up to the mirror mounts, and where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.

questions.question: If asked to back your vehicle into an alley, you should first:

options.text: Pull directly into the alley space.
Turn right to position yourself in front of the alley.
Pull past the alley and stop perpendicular to the outer boundary.
Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary.
questions.explanation: First, pull past the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary. Then back your vehicle into the alley. Your vehicle should be straight and inside the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: An active railroad crossing:

options.text: Has traffic control devices at the crossing.
Has no traffic control devices.
Has at least 10 vehicles cross the tracks every hour.
Should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has traffic control devices at the crossing.
questions.explanation: Active railroad crossings have traffic control devices like flashing red lights, bells, or gates. You must always follow these devices.

questions.question: School bus stops can only be changed by:

options.text: The driver.
Parents.
The school district.
Students.

questions.correctAnswerText: The school district.
questions.explanation: A driver cannot change a stop without written approval from the school district.

questions.question: When stopping to pick up students, a bus driver should:

options.text: Put the vehicle in park.
Put the vehicle in first gear.
Put the vehicle in reverse.
Put the vehicle in third gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in park.
questions.explanation: Put the bus in park when stopping to pick up students. If there is no park gear, use neutral instead.

questions.question: The overhead inside rearview mirror should show:

options.text: The rear tires.
All students on the bus.
The floor of the bus.
The ceiling of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: All students on the bus.
questions.explanation: The overhead mirror helps the driver watch students inside the bus. Position it so you can see all students, including those sitting right behind the driver.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test:

options.text: Points are lost for each pull-up.
You are allowed three pull-ups per maneuver.
A pull-up earns points only if you get out of the vehicle first.
Only too many pull-ups count as errors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only too many pull-ups count as errors.
questions.explanation: One or two pull-ups do not count against you. Only an excessive number of pull-ups counts as errors.

questions.question: Blind spots are found ____ the left and right side flat mirrors.

options.text: Right below
In the middle of
Above
To the left of

questions.correctAnswerText: Right below
questions.explanation: Blind spots are located right below and in front of each outside flat mirror. There is also a blind spot directly behind the rear bumper.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, lug nuts must be all of the following, except:

options.text: Free of cracks.
Free of distortions.
Loose.
Free of rust.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loose.
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection, lug nuts must be present and tight. They must be free of cracks, distortions, and rust. All bolt holes must also be free of cracks and distortions.

questions.question: For a driver's side parallel parking test, you should:

options.text: Pass the space while backing, then pull forward into it.
Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
Pull forward into the space without passing it first.
Back into the space without passing it first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space on your left. Then back into it, bringing the rear of your vehicle as close to the back of the space as possible. Your vehicle must be completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: The area to the left of a school bus is dangerous to students because:

options.text: The sun's reflection blocks the view of the left side.
Other vehicles pass on the left side.
The left side of any bus is hard to see.
There is no door on the left side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Other vehicles pass on the left side.
questions.explanation: The left side of a school bus is especially dangerous for students because passing vehicles travel on that side.

questions.question: Before starting a trip, check that:

options.text: The pedal surface is smooth.
The gas pedal sticks.
Nothing blocks the pedals.
Something is under the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing blocks the pedals.
questions.explanation: Check that nothing is under or around the pedals that could get in the way. Make sure the pedals work properly and have grooved surfaces if they should.

questions.question: Properly adjusted outside curved mirrors should let the driver see:

options.text: Where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.
Where the front of each front tire touches the ground.
The top of the bus.
The muffler.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.
questions.explanation: Outside curved mirrors should be adjusted so the driver can see at least one traffic lane on each side of the bus, the entire side of the bus, and where the front of each rear tire touches the ground.

questions.question: Passive railroad crossings:

options.text: Have control devices.
Do not have control devices.
Should be avoided.
Usually have a person directing traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not have control devices.
questions.explanation: Passive railroad crossings have no traffic control devices. The driver is responsible for deciding when it is safe to cross the tracks.

questions.question: If your bus's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) fails:

options.text: You will lose all braking power.
The brakes will work slower than normal.
You will still have normal braking power.
You should not use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will still have normal braking power.
questions.explanation: If the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops working, the vehicle keeps its normal braking power. Drive and brake normally.

questions.question: When approaching a curve on the road test, you must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Check traffic in all directions.
Slow down before entering the curve.
Keep your vehicle in its lane.
Keep using the brakes while in the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep using the brakes while in the curve.
questions.explanation: When approaching a curve, check traffic in all directions. Slow down enough before the curve so you do not need to brake inside it. Stay in your lane and keep checking traffic.

questions.question: Crossover mirrors help a school bus driver see:

options.text: The danger zones near the front bumper.
The rear bumper.
The left side of the bus.
Vehicles in front of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The danger zones near the front bumper.
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors help the driver see the danger zone directly in front of the bus. They also show the danger zones on the left and right sides, from the front of the bus to the service door.
